pull.title: util, cli: name the Sock wait timeout cap and use it for -rpcclienttimeout=0
pull.body:
Follow-up to #36340, addressing the review comments from pinheadmz and winterrdog there.

#36340 capped the `Sock::Wait`/`WaitMany` timeout at `INT_MAX` milliseconds (about 24.8 days) inside `WaitMany`. This moves that value to a named constant, `Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, and mentions the cap in the doxygen comments of `Wait()` and `WaitMany()`, since it applies to every caller and not only to `bitcoin-cli`. The constant is a whole number of seconds (2147483 s), so `bitcoin-cli`, which works in seconds, uses exactly the same value as `Sock`.

`bitcoin-cli` still turned `-rpcclienttimeout=0` into a 5 year timeout. The timeout is applied to each wait for the socket, and each wait is now capped, so in practice `0` already means "give up after about 24.8 days without data". The 5 year value is replaced with `Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, and the help text now says that 0 is the longest supported timeout (about 24 days) instead of no timeout.

There is no behaviour change. `sock_tests`, `interface_bitcoin_cli.py` (including the `-rpcclienttimeout=0` call added in #36340) and `interface_rpc.py` pass on macOS.

(Changes prepared with AI tools.)

the help text that 0 means the longest supported timeout (about 24 days)
instead of no timeout.

comments.body:
not sure about the cast here. this will again lead to two (minimally) different values in the cli and in the sock impl. the goal of this pull should be to fix this. Either:

* Cast `MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT` to seconds.
* Extend the precision here to have the exact same value.

Otherwise, there will be an obscure platform in the future where this is silently broken again.

Done, went with the first option: `MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT` is now a `std::chrono::seconds` (INT_MAX ms truncated to whole seconds, 2147483 s), so the cli uses it directly without a cast and both use exactly the same value. `WaitMany` converts it to milliseconds for the `std::min`.

comments.body:
_non-blocking nit_: could we say "_maximum timeout_" rather than "_longest timeout_", since longer requested timeouts are capped to this value ?

this is what i had in mind (feel free to put a spin to it however you like):

```suggestion
    /**
     * Maximum timeout supported by `Wait()` and `WaitMany()` (about 24.8 days).
     * Longer timeouts are capped because `poll()` takes an `int` timeout in
     * milliseconds, and `select()` rejects large timeouts on some platforms
     * (e.g. macOS). Expressed in seconds so that callers can use the same value.
     */
```

"_whole number_" is missing because `std::chrono::seconds` is a signed _integer_ of at least 35 bits i.e. `std::chrono::duration</* int35 */>` (see "_Helper types_" section in https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/chrono/duration)
